content:
The 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election took place on May 3, 2012. The council is located in Greater Manchester, England. In this election, all 63 seats on the council were up for election.

The Labour Party made significant gains in this election, winning 12 additional seats compared to the previous election in 2011. They secured 30 seats in total, becoming the largest party on the council. The Liberal Democrats lost 14 seats and were reduced to 25 seats overall. The Conservative Party also lost seats, dropping to 8 in total.

There were also independent candidates who won 2 seats and the Heald Green Ratepayers Association won 5 seats. The Greens won 1 seat on the council.

The turnout for the election was 36.1%, slightly lower than the previous election.

Overall, the 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election resulted in a change in control of the council, with Labour taking over from the Liberal Democrats as the largest party. This marked a significant shift in the political landscape of Stockport.
